label: Parity, symmetric form: a feature-uniform demand excludes accepting an unreasoned fact (inference)
rule: Uniformity transfers the demand along the shared feature; the demand met excludes having no reason
meaning: The owner's parity argument in its symmetric form, analyst formulation, attribution deferred. Under the same P1-P3, the stance requires a reason why o obtains, so meeting its demand it cannot accept o with no reason, whether o is contingent or necessary. It binds a naturalist who rejects an unreasoned God (target God, o the contingent foundation) and a theist who rejects unreasoned contingents (target a contingent existent, o God's existence) alike (parity map, both instances). With unreasoned existence rejected on both sides, what remains is a comparison of explanations of existence, which this argument does not settle: it needs an open comparative principle (#750) and the open adequacy of a self-reason. It establishes neither B2 nor that anything has a reason, and it does not answer whether there is evidence for God.
